statement.text:
A group G is said to be stable if for any first-order formula ϕ(x̄, ȳ) (in the
first-order language of groups { · , −1 , 1}) there exists a natural number n such that
whenever there exist sequences of tuples of G, (ai )i<m , (bi )i<m with G |= ϕ(ai , bj ) if
and only if i < j, then m ⩽ n. Sela proved that all torsion-free hyperbolic groups are
stable.
     a) Is there a non-stable hyperbolic group?
     b) Is there a non-stable virtually free group?
     c) Is SL2 (Z) non-stable?                                                R. Sklinos
